high.title: Ringgit ends higher on weaker US dollar sentiment
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened against the US dollar as safe-haven demand eased following reports of continued US-Iran peace negotiations despite military escalation. Bank Negara Malaysia's decision to hold the OPR unchanged at 2.75% was in line with expectations, providing a neutral but stable policy backdrop. Easing oil prices further supported the ringgit by signalling markets are not pricing in prolonged geopolitical escalation.

high.title: Bursa closes higher on rebound in financial stocks
high.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 13.85 points (0.83%) to close at 1,691.49, driven by a rebound in financial stocks and positive market breadth. BNM's decision to maintain the OPR at 2.75% provided policy certainty for investors amid global energy price concerns. Turnover improved to RM2.25 billion, reflecting renewed investor confidence.

high.title: Ringgit closes flat as FOMC minutes weigh on US dollar
high.summary: BNM's MPC maintained the OPR at 2.75% for the seventh consecutive period, reinforcing policy stability for 2026. The FOMC minutes revealed Fed officials are divided between holding or raising rates, with no cuts on the table, keeping the FFR at 3.50%-3.75%. This dual policy certainty from both BNM and the Fed has a direct impact on ringgit valuation and Malaysian capital flows.

high.title: Bursa closes lower amid renewed geopolitical tensions
high.summary: Bursa Malaysia closed lower as escalating US-Iran tensions following consecutive US strikes on Iranian targets raised concerns over global energy supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the index decline, market breadth improved with gainers leading across multiple sectors, indicating selective resilience. BNM's decision to hold the OPR at 2.75% provided some policy certainty to cushion investor sentiment.

high.title: Ringgit rises as Fed minutes weigh on US dollar
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0730 against the USD as FOMC minutes revealed a wider divide among Fed officials on future rate direction, weakening the US Dollar Index. Fed officials are now debating between holding or raising the current FFR of 3.50%-3.75%, with rate cuts no longer under consideration. This shift in Fed outlook has direct implications for Malaysian currency positioning and cross-border investment decisions.

high.title: Bursa gives up gains on renewed Middle East uncertainty
high.summary: The FBM KLCI slipped 2.20 points at opening to 1,681.41 as renewed Middle East tensions, triggered by Trump's announcement that the ceasefire with Iran had ended, dampened investor sentiment. Wall Street closed mixed overnight, reflecting the same geopolitical uncertainty that is spilling into regional markets including Bursa. Energy supply risks through the Strait of Hormuz could have downstream effects on Malaysia's trade-dependent economy.

high.title: BNM may hold policy rate, signal upcoming hike as AI boosts economic growth
high.summary: Bank Negara Malaysia is expected to keep its overnight policy rate at 2.75% at its 3pm decision, with 24 of 25 economists surveyed by Bloomberg forecasting no change. Malaysia stands out among Southeast Asian peers as Indonesia and Philippines have been forced to aggressively hike rates due to currency weakness and inflation driven by the Iran war. The AI-driven export boom is providing a buffer for Malaysia's growth and inflation outlook, reducing pressure to tighten monetary policy.

high.title: Ringgit eases against US dollar as Middle East tensions rise
high.summary: The ringgit weakened against the US dollar to 4.0745/4.0830 following US military strikes on Iranian forces and the revocation of Iran's oil export waiver, triggering risk-off sentiment in global markets. Brent crude surged over 6% to US$76.40 per barrel, raising concerns about supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz. The currency did strengthen against other major currencies including the yen, pound, and euro, reflecting a broadly dollar-driven move.

high.title: Ringgit ends higher as weaker greenback, firmer oil lift sentiment
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0685/4.0735 against the US dollar at close, driven by a weaker greenback and firmer oil prices. US ISM services PMI easing to 54.0 supported Asian currencies amid uncertain Fed rate hike expectations. Markets are awaiting the FOMC meeting minutes for further guidance on the Fed's interest rate outlook.

high.title: Ringgit slips as investors return to US dollar after weak jobs report
high.summary: The ringgit eased to 4.0825/4.0875 against the greenback as investors returned to the US dollar following a weak jobs report. Caution prevailed ahead of the Fed's June meeting minutes release, with broader Asian currencies also weakening. The US ISM services index for June was a key data point being monitored by market participants.

medium.title: Bursa rises as tech stocks lift Wall Street sentiment
medium.summary: Bursa Malaysia opened higher, with the FBM KLCI rising 0.48% to 1,685.64, buoyed by an overnight Wall Street rebound led by tech stocks and easing crude oil prices. Positive market breadth at the open with gainers outnumbering decliners 208 to 85 signalled broad-based optimism. This early session data provides context for the day's full market performance.

medium.title: Ringgit gains ground against US dollar amid geopolitical caution
medium.summary: The ringgit opened stronger at 4.0720 against the US dollar, supported by BNM's MPC statement indicating Malaysia's economy is on a stronger footing. Strong electrical and electronics export growth linked to global AI and technology investment was highlighted as a key confidence driver for the currency. The ringgit also appreciated against major currencies including the yen, pound, and euro.

medium.title: Boeing unveils new 737 MAX production line as aviation giant charts comeback
medium.summary: Boeing has launched a new US$1 billion '737 MAX North Line' production facility in Everett, Washington, signalling a strategic capacity expansion for its flagship commercial aircraft. The gradual ramp-up plan reflects continued caution following two deadly MAX crashes, but marks an important step in Boeing's recovery that could affect Malaysian airlines operating or ordering the MAX. Increased MAX production capacity may influence future aircraft procurement decisions and aviation sector dynamics in the region.

medium.title: UST partners with Anthropic to help Global 1000 firms become AI-native
medium.summary: UST has partnered with Anthropic to embed Claude AI into operational workflows for the world's 1,000 largest publicly traded companies across healthcare, telecommunications, and banking sectors. The partnership involves deploying up to 20,000 associates to guide AI adoption, which could have implications for Malaysian enterprises in these sectors seeking AI integration. This reflects the growing enterprise AI adoption trend relevant to tech and digital transformation investments in Malaysia.

medium.title: Ringgit ends higher against major currencies but slips versus US dollar
medium.summary: Brent crude surged 5.68% to US$78.28 per barrel by end of day as US military attacks on Iranian forces and the revocation of Iran's oil export waiver stoked fears of Strait of Hormuz disruptions. Markets are also bracing for the release of FOMC minutes on July 9, which could further influence global risk appetite and currency movements. The dual pressure of geopolitical risk and US monetary policy signals remains a key concern for ringgit stability.

medium.title: Bursa ends higher on late buying interest
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI closed marginally higher at 1,683.61, recovering from intraday lows as late institutional buying offset earlier pressure from rising oil prices and Middle East geopolitical tensions. Domestic sentiment proved resilient despite a broadly risk-off mood across Asian markets stemming from US airstrikes on Iran. Investors are closely monitoring energy prices and global interest rate implications as the Iran conflict evolves.

medium.title: Bursa opens higher, outperforms regional peers
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened 0.38% higher at 1,689.35, outperforming regional peers despite Wall Street closing lower on concerns that market valuations had outpaced fundamentals, with AI-related stocks selling off. Fresh attacks in the Strait of Hormuz pushed Brent crude to around US$74 per barrel at the open, while US 10-year Treasury yields edged up to 4.551%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng also slipped below 23,500 as AI stock weakness spread across Asian markets.

medium.title: Bursa ends marginally lower on mild profit-taking
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI eased 0.60 of a point to close at 1,682.93, reflecting mild profit-taking after recent gains. Analysts described the decline as normal consolidation rather than a sentiment reversal, with the index holding above recent lows. Markets are expected to remain supported by easing geopolitical tensions and resilient global risk appetite.

medium.title: Bursa slips after recent gains as sellers return
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI slipped 4.01 points or 0.24% to 1,679.52 in early trade as sellers returned following recent gains. Market breadth was slightly negative with decliners outpacing gainers, reflecting a cautious undertone among investors. Rakuten Trade noted that despite Monday's firmer close, market sentiment remained guarded.

medium.title: Ringgit opens slightly higher amid focus on Fed outlook
medium.summary: The ringgit opened slightly higher at 4.0815/4.0880 against the US dollar, though it weakened against most other major currencies. Fed Governor Waller's reaffirmation of the 2% inflation target signaled a higher-for-longer rate stance, keeping the US dollar supported. Investors remained focused on upcoming Fed guidance as a key driver for ringgit direction.
